LOVELAND, Ohio (WKRC) - Leaders in a Tri-State community are launching a campaign to bring a new feature to one of its parks.

Loveland wants to bring an iconic ode to the city's cryptid history to Nisbet Park. It would be in celebration of Loveland's 150th anniversary.

The campaign would add a bronze sculpture inspired by Loveland's longtime connection to the elusive "Frogman."

As it stands, the sculpture does not have a name, and the community is being invited to help bring the project to life.

The first modern sighting of a 4-foot frog on two legs was reported in the 1950s. Riverside Drive was believed to be the site of two close calls in the 1970s.

The Loveland Frogman stands out from other cryptids because of its reputation. Unlike other popular cryptids, the Loveland Frog has no negative connotation or any "dark sides" to it.
